title: Al-Hajjaj and the Courageous Young Sayyid

full_text:
The formidable and stern governor Al-Hajjaj bin Yusuf sat in his audience hall in Kufa, surrounded by armored guards with drawn scimitars. A young descendant of the Prophet's house, a youth of sixteen named Sayyid Yahya, was brought before him in chains, accused of speaking publicly against the governor's harsh taxes.

Al-Hajjaj fixed him with a piercing gaze and said:
'Boy, dost thou not know that my word commands death and life in this province? What madness drove thee to speak against my authority?'

Sayyid Yahya stood erect, his chains clinking softly, but his eyes were clear, steady, and devoid of fear:
'O Governor, life and death are held solely in the hands of the Almighty, who created thee from dust and will return thee to dust. Thy authority is a temporary trust; if thou usest it to crush the weak and extract sweat from the poor, thy power is not majesty, but a heavy debt thou must pay on the Day of Reckoning.'

The courtiers gasped at the youth's boldness, expecting the executioner's blade to fall.
Al-Hajjaj's brow darkened with thunder:
'Art thou not afraid of this sword?'

Yahya replied with serene eloquence:
'Why should I fear the sword that can only sever a mortal neck, while neglecting to fear the Lord who can punish an unjust soul for eternity?
A ruler who listens only to flattery is like a sick man who drinks honey mixed with poison. The truest loyalty a subject can show his governor is to remind him of justice when wrath blinds his judgment.'

Al-Hajjaj sat in silence for a long time. The fierce governor, known for unyielding ruthlessness, was struck to the heart by the boy's moral courage, eloquence, and unshakeable faith.

Slowly, Al-Hajjaj raised his hand:
'Strike off his chains! By Allah, I have heard ten thousand courtiers sing my praises, but none possessed the courage of this youth. A kingdom that silences voices like his is already doomed.'

Al-Hajjaj rewarded the young Sayyid with gifts, revoked the oppressive tax on the district, and allowed Yahya to depart with highest honors, demonstrating that unyielding truth spoken without fear has power to soften iron hearts.
moral: Truth spoken with fearless eloquence and spiritual dignity disarms the fiercest tyrants.
